title: Requested port-source groundwork discovery
summary: Add fourteen requested game-source, format-research and patch projects with explicit limits; defer four emulation-based or redesigned games.
notes: Root personally searched C64, Spectrum, Amiga, ST, CPC and DOS candidates and followed the explicitly requested console/arcade port-source wishlist. Fourteen additions distinguish rebuildable-source claims, partial listings, format tools, semantic engine reconstruction, binary course patches and public-only metadata. Four emulation/redesign candidates remain deferred, alongside four external port/subsystem research leads requiring a focused source-package audit. No discovery worker used. No upstream binaries, emulators, build scripts or asset pipelines executed. Reported completeness is scoped and not independently verified. Source bytes remain ephemeral local evidence; retained input contains only immutable proof identities.

sources.reason: Sixteen-bank Konami4 reconstruction with flow-derived listings, anchored commentary, mapper analysis and reported whole-ROM matching. All bytes classified does not mean all behavior understood: late-stage tables, slot-machine timing, a BIOS-specific startup failure and sound-player extraction remain open.

RC-712 16 KB listing includes named VRAM routines and data ownership, with reported pasmo byte match and graphics comparison against openMSX. Act order after the lion, moving-object flags and difficulty counters remain incompletely understood.

Large main assembly listing plus split animation, map and behavior tables, an IDA database and build script. RNC-compressed data is separated for extraction/repacking. Exact reconstruction and semantic completeness are not independently established.

Routine-by-routine engine code implements rooms, actors, menus and the original game-script VM. Original RAM layout is deliberately retained because scripts address engine variables; no general 68000 CPU is exposed in the inspected machine interface. Software VDP and Z80/FM/PSG sound models remain, so this is not a hardware-independent Amiga-ready engine.

Small standalone C decoder implements Rocket Knight Adventures LZSS with a 1 KB history dictionary, literal/back-reference packets and stored length checks. It recovers an asset format, not gameplay code.

Maps sound IDs, sequencers and chip behavior separately for CPS-1 arcade and Mega Drive. Uses original drivers under MAME to render synthesized music/effects, rather than claiming the sounds are all stored PCM. Includes static disassembly and sample decoders; looping captures do not recover loop semantics.

Single Bank $00 listing exposes startup, mapper writes, dual-video initialization and dispatch. Many raw addresses and cross-bank calls remain; there is no complete ROM reconstruction or build framework in the inspected tree.

A 2.4 MB IDA-derived assembly listing has some named routines but substantial generic labels and raw data. README says this restarts an earlier lost project. No current matching-build or full semantic-analysis claim is established.

Decodes PH containers, backgrounds, palettes, sprite banks and animation scripts. Handoff is ahead of README: browser has Harry walking/jumping and named animations, but no entities, hazards, pickups or level transitions. Movement constants are invented and the collision-bit interpretation is inferred, not traced to the original collision test.

Documents PAK/TLK, CPS/SHP/WSA, audio/text, EMC2 and the CMZ-WLL-VMP-VCN level pipeline, with public extraction/rendering scripts. Authors near-100-percent closure claim concerns this extraction/documentation lane, not recovery of a complete executable engine.
Banked assembly, object and collision/HP tables support JP, US and EU revisions; README reports identical ROM assembly. Prototype revisions remain unchecked.

Structured SNES bank/data disassembly includes US/European build choices, an SPC700 engine assembly step, ROM maps and asset extraction scripts. These files establish a concrete reconstruction workflow, not an independently verified matching result here.

Public function/symbol maps, data-region and indirect-target evidence, methodology and auditing tools. README explicitly withholds recovered assembly and rebuild pipeline; its 100-percent classification and byte-exact claims refer to a non-public corpus and cannot be reproduced from this checkout.

IPS patch release transplants the Neo Geo CD Scotland course into MVS/AES by replacing Australia. Includes course graphics/maps, selection sound and fixes for collisions and scorecards. Public deliverable is binary patches and documentation, not a full disassembly.

Desktop static recompilation using the Genesis hardware/runtime framework, not a semantic hardware-independent engine. Record as a game-specific recompilation audit candidate; source tools like Clownacy RKA decompressor are tracked separately.

Explicitly SNES, not the arcade PCB version. Current README says execution uses the low-level interpreter bridge despite native-port branding. Do not promote as recovered native game source or Amiga port.

Extensive instruction-to-C reconstruction retains 65816 register/flag state, interpreter fallback and SNES PPU/APU models. Useful related work but game-specific emulation/recompilation remains outside normal native-restoration additions.
README explicitly describes a newly written, modified AD&D-inspired dungeon crawler rather than a reconstruction of Eye of the Beholder III: Assault on Myth Drannor. Avoid title-based false positive.

Current official page offers an HDF and states AGA, 68030 and 8 MB RAM; stale page metadata and older coverage say 32 MB. No public source located or binary tested, so retain as a port lead rather than a verified source reconstruction.
Official package describes included source for the WHDLoad loader/patch. This is not publication of the complete Utopia game engine; retain narrow loader research lead.

Author documents moving HuC6280 enemy-bullet collision logic into 68000 code and offers source with an IPS release. Concrete subsystem research, not proof of completed Amiga conversion; downloadable source package not audited in this pass.
Primary site exposes partial cclimber.asm, memory map, building and graphics notes and labels the analysis 1 percent. Preserve for focused source audit; not a complete game or Amiga conversion.
